title: 睡过头了  (Oversleeping in the Dorm)

segments.t: Back in their Media College dorm room, exhausted Bu Xiaogu wakes up late in the morning after her roommate Qin Xiao let her sleep through her alarm. Listen to their conversation first.
啊？已经十一点了！
秦箫，你怎么不叫我呀？
我发誓，我叫了你一百遍了。
好吧，后来想想还是算了。
你最近太累了，应该多睡一会儿。
你想吃什么？
我去给你买。
不用了，我现在没时间吃饭。
昨晚我又不小心睡着了。
我的论文还没写完呢。
今天上班还迟到了！
那你快去吧，路上小心！
Let's unpack what they say. Xiaogu bolts upright in bed the moment she checks the clock.
啊？已经十一点了！
'What? It is already eleven!' Clock hours in Mandarin simply pair the number with "dian", 'o'clock', so "shiyi dian" is 'eleven', and "yijing ... le" underscores how late it has gotten.
秦箫，你怎么不叫我呀？
'Qin Xiao, how come you did not wake me up?' Everyday "jiao" means both 'call' and 'wake someone up', while soft final "ya" keeps the complaint playful between friends.
我发誓，我叫了你一百遍了。
'I swear, I called you a hundred times.' Opening with "wo fashi" means 'I swear', and "yibai bian" counts a hundred full rounds of trying to wake her.
好吧，后来想想还是算了。
'Alright, on second thought I decided to let it go.' Conceding with "haoba" admits the truth, and versatile "suanle" shrugs off an effort with 'forget it' or 'let it be'.
你最近太累了，应该多睡一会儿。
'You have been too tired lately and should sleep a bit longer.' Putting "duo", 'more', right before the action in "duo shui yihuir" is how Mandarin says 'sleep a little longer'.
你想吃什么？
'What would you like to eat?' Notice how Mandarin leaves the question word in place: "ni xiang chi shenme" literally runs 'you want eat what'.
我去给你买。
'I will go buy it for you.' Slipping "gei ni", 'for you', ahead of "mai", 'buy', is the standard way to offer to pick something up for someone.
不用了，我现在没时间吃饭。
'No need, I have no time to eat right now.' Polite "buyong le" declines an offer warmly, and "mei shijian" is the go-to chunk for having no time.
昨晚我又不小心睡着了。
'Last night I accidentally fell asleep again.' Literally "bu xiaoxin" says 'not careful' for doing something by accident, and "shuizhao" adds "zhao" onto "shui" to mean 'fall asleep'.
我的论文还没写完呢。
'My thesis is still not finished yet.' Framing an unfinished task with "hai mei ... ne" means 'still have not yet', while "xiewan" joins 'write' with 'finish'.
今天上班还迟到了！
'And I am late for work today too!' Going to work is "shangban", literally 'step onto shift', and "chidao" is the everyday word for 'arrive late'.
那你快去吧，路上小心！
'Then hurry off, and take care on the way!' Friends say "lushang xiaoxin", literally 'careful on the road', whenever someone dashes out the door. Now let us hear the whole conversation once more.
啊？已经十一点了！
秦箫，你怎么不叫我呀？
我发誓，我叫了你一百遍了。
好吧，后来想想还是算了。
你最近太累了，应该多睡一会儿。
你想吃什么？
我去给你买。
不用了，我现在没时间吃饭。
昨晚我又不小心睡着了。
我的论文还没写完呢。
今天上班还迟到了！
那你快去吧，路上小心！

Xiaogu rushes out of the dorm late for studio prep with her graduation thesis still unfinished. You learned how to tell the hour with "dian", say you fell asleep with "shuizhao", and talk about being late for work with "shangban chidao". See you next time!
回头见！
